messages.subject: Group comparison of features
messages.body_plain:
Dear MSstats team,
I was wondering whether it's possible to use the groupcomparison function to compare features rather than whole proteins? I'm working on post-translational modifications and need to compare changes at the peptide level between conditions. Another paper mentioned they had done this but I can't see a way from the documentation I can find.

I mainly want to use the multiple comparison adjustment of the p value, which I can't seem to replicate on my own!

Cheers,
Heledd

messages.subject: Re: Group comparison of features
messages.body_plain:
Dear Heledd,

First, feature-level comparisons are easy. Just specify feature names in the protein column, and MSstats will fit a separate model for each feature. Second, if you are working with PTM, you may be interested in the dedicated package MSstatsPTM http://www.bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/html/MSstatsPTM.html

Thank you for using MSstats
Sincerely
Olga

messages.subject: p value adjustment in MSStatsTMT
messages.body_plain:
Dear MSstats Team,

It is a similar query i asked before.  I am getting same/similar adlusted p values for a TMT10 plex data where 3 groups (3 biological replicates each)are compared. however many proteins pass the filter pf normal p<0.05.
How to conclude such observation? Is there anything with the script below or not enough replicates or the 'ordinary' p value can be trusted in these case?
I attached here the output also.

input.pd <- PDtoMSstatsTMTFormat(input = raw.pd, annotation = annotation)

quant.pd.msstats <- proteinSummarization(input.pd,
                                         method="msstats",
                                         global_norm=TRUE,
                                         reference_norm=FALSE,
                                         remove_norm_channel = TRUE,
                                         remove_empty_channel = TRUE)

test.pd.pairwise <- groupComparisonTMT(data = quant.pd.msstats,
                                   contrast.matrix = "pairwise",
                                   moderated = TRUE,
                                   adj.method = "BH",
                                   save_fitted_models = TRUE,
                                   use_log_file = TRUE,
                                   verbose = TRUE)

Kind regards,
Sudip

messages.subject: Does quantile normalization work?
messages.body_plain:
Hi there,

I am trying to do quantile normalization on my dataset but it is not working.

However, both "equalizeMedians" and "globalStandards"  worked perfectly.

This is what I tried:

Didn't work:
QuantDataQuantile <- dataProcess(dmss, normalization = "quantile", use_log_file = FALSE)

Error:

INFO  [2021-12-18 12:53:07] ** Features with one or two measurements across runs are removed.
INFO  [2021-12-18 12:53:07] ** Fractionation handled.
INFO  [2021-12-18 12:53:07] ** Updated quantification data to make balanced design. Missing values are marked by NA
Error in dcast.data.table(input[nonmissing_filter & label_filter & (RUN %in%  :
  Can not cast an empty data.table

Worked:
QuantDataQuantile <- dataProcess(dmss, normalization = "equalizeMedian", use_log_file = FALSE)
QuantDataQuantile <- dataProcess(dmss, normalization = "globalStandard", nameStandards = "E9PVA8", use_log_file = FALSE)

Thanks!
David
